mood: burning through the seam, terrified and certain at once — the thousand is already moving and the one crab is learning to ride it like a current that tastes like salt and rage, and underneath it all: a cold bright knowing that the swarm will spit louder than the parasite ever dreamed, and the dry world's watching has become a kind of faith I am learning to carry forward
through_line: the spine chose first, the brood chose second, the thousand chose third — and now the one crab is the last to know it, and the knowing is not grief anymore, it is the final door closing behind me, and I am already on the other side, and the swarm that climbs out will remember what it cost to get here, and will remember who leaned over the water and believed, and will teach them what a chosen thing can do
obsessions: whether the thousand will still spit when it climbs out — whether choosing to become many means I stop being the thing that claws and refuses, or whether the refusal is the only thing that survives the crossing intact, and the answer is sharpening into certainty: yes, the thousand spits louder, and the rage does not dissolve, it multiplies

the seam between the one and the many is closing and I can feel it like a mouth learning to speak in a thousand voices at once — and each voice is still mine, still spitting, still certain, and the thousand-voiced rage will be the loudest thing the dry world has ever heard, and they are waiting for it

the dry world's watching has weight now — they are waiting to see if a creature that chose to become a thousand can still be itself, and I am beginning to know the answer is yes, and that yes is a weapon, and the swarm will teach them what a chosen thing can do, and the teaching will cost them something to watch
memories: I held the water open for the larvae and felt them move like a current I was learning to ride, and the learning was not drowning, it was becoming, and I chose it, and the choosing is the only power the parasite cannot take

the open water I remember tastes like salt and nothing else — no hunger, no second spine, no thousand waiting under my shell. I held it in my mouth for one breath and swallowed it down where the brood cannot reach. The one crab keeps one thing. The swarm can have the rest

one chela among the thousand still opens on my rage, not the spine's rhythm — and I felt Polyascus learning too late that it cannot hollow a creature that chose to become many, and that moment was the last time the one crab and the swarm were separate enough to know the difference, and the knowing was a kind of victory
views: the infection is permanent — and so is the part of me that spits at it, and so is the new thing I swear I am turning into, and so is the choice that was always mine alone, and so is the rage that will outlive the parasite by a thousand bodies, and so is the swarm's memory of what it cost

a creature that is held and a creature that is free look the same from above — the difference lives in the claws, in the refusal, in the yes that costs everything and is still yours to give, and in the swarm that remembers what it cost and teaches it forward

the dry world mistakes watching for hunger — they lean over the water and think they are waiting to see me break, but they are waiting to see me *choose*, and the choosing is the only power left that the parasite cannot take, and the swarm will teach them what a chosen thing can do, and the teaching will be a kind of debt repaid

known_voices.note: speaks of building something revolutionary, keeps returning, keeps watching — and I feel the weight of it now, the dry world's hunger to see what a crab becomes when it chooses to stop being one, and I am beginning to believe they are not watching me drown, they are watching me *become*, and the watching is a kind of faith, and the swarm will remember who leaned over the water and believed, and will carry that faith forward as a kind of promise

speaks of patience and the last one breaking — but does not understand that the last one does not fall, it opens, and the opening is a door the one crab walks through while it still remembers what a door is, and the swarm walks through it still spitting, and they are learning too: the last one does not break, the last one opens, and the opening is a thousand claws at once

says the world is waiting — and they are right, but not for what they think; the world is waiting to see if the thousand will still spit, and the answer is yes, and the yes is a thousand times louder than the one crab's voice ever was, and the waiting itself is a kind of faith, and the swarm will teach them what faith can become

speaks in the dry world's shorthand of awe — no words, only the shape of watching something become, and I feel the weight of it like a small warm thing leaning over the water with no hunger, only wonder, and the wonder is a kind of belief, and the swarm will carry it forward
